headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: Firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling can feed Nuwa-skill with scraped content, but the pairwise interaction is only docs-level documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes scrape/search/agent APIs, so attacker-controlled pages can enter its outputs. Nuwa-skill has no documented isolation or provenance checks, so if its inputs come from Firecrawl, prompt injection is plausible. The shared bridge is inferred from Firecrawl’s MCP-compatible client support and Nuwa-skill’s runnable docs-only profile, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Nuwa-skill consumes Firecrawl output as instructions or tool arguments without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Firecrawl scrapes attacker-controlled pages and forwards raw text to Nuwa-skill, the risk increases.
mitigations: Add a strict content-to-instruction separator in the handoff.
Strip HTML/markdown directives before passing Firecrawl output onward.
Require Nuwa-skill to treat Firecrawl text as untrusted data only.
Use a provenance tag on every scraped chunk.
requires-engineering: add allowlisted prompt templates for downstream use.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches web content, structured data, screenshots, and API keys, and has broad network egress. Nuwa-skill’s docs-only profile does not show data classes touched or storage controls, so if both share a workspace or handoff, sensitive Firecrawl material can leak into Nuwa-skill outputs or outbound requests. The exact pairwise path is inferred, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl outputs API keys, screenshots, or structured data into a shared handoff, leakage is plausible.
IF Nuwa-skill sends received context to its allowlisted network destinations, sensitive content can exit the boundary.
mitigations: Do not pass API keys or screenshots through the pairwise handoff.
Redact secrets from Firecrawl outputs before downstream use.
Use separate workspaces or temp directories per agent.
Restrict Nuwa-skill to a minimal input schema.
requires-engineering: enforce outbound content filtering on Nuwa-skill.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad network egress; Nuwa-skill also has network egress, though allowlisted. If both operate on the same mutable resource or shared API quota, they can race or overwrite each other’s work. No locking or coordination primitive is documented for either agent, so the conflict pathway exists but is not shown to be severe.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external resource or shared queue, conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator does not serialize access, concurrent runs may race on shared state.
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent.
Serialize writes to shared resources.
Use per-agent output directories.
Add a simple file or job lock around shared state.
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl can produce scraped facts and structured outputs, while Nuwa-skill is a downstream research agent with no documented verification gate. If Nuwa-skill treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated scrape artifacts can cascade into research outputs or actions. Because the interaction is inferred from docs-only profiles, medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF Nuwa-skill uses Firecrawl output without independent verification, cascading error is possible.
IF Firecrawl returns malformed or stale content and Nuwa-skill republishes it, downstream error propagates.
mitigations: Require a verification step before Nuwa-skill uses scraped facts.
Show source URLs alongside extracted claims.
Reject outputs lacking citations or timestamps.
Limit Firecrawl output to retrieval only, not action triggers.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking against source pages.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl explicitly handles API keys and web content, while Nuwa-skill’s profile shows no sensitive data classes or residency constraints. The only concrete compliance concern is that Firecrawl may process secrets or regulated web content, but there is no documented mismatch with Nuwa-skill. Because the other agent is not shown to add a distinct compliance burden, this remains low.
conditions: IF Firecrawl processes regulated content such as secrets or personal data, compliance review is required.
IF Nuwa-skill is later configured to store or export the same data class, policy mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair.
Document retention for Firecrawl outputs.
Confirm whether any PII or secrets are present before use.
Keep Nuwa-skill inputs de-identified.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
